questions.q: Only 0.67% of transactions are fraud. Why is accuracy a poor metric?
options: A model that always predicts 'legitimate' would be about 99.3% accurate while catching no fraud
Accuracy cannot be computed on imbalanced data
Accuracy is only valid for regression
Accuracy always equals recall
questions.explain: With such rare positives, the majority-class answer scores very high accuracy without finding any fraud, so accuracy hides failure.

options: The average of predicted probabilities
The proportion of rows in the majority class
How well the model ranks positives, summarizing the precision-recall curve
The difference between train and test loss
questions.explain: Average precision summarizes precision across recall levels. It is sensitive to how well rare positives are ranked, and its no-skill baseline is the base rate.

questions.q: Why did the walkthrough write a manual cross-validation loop for the weighted model?
options: cross_val_score cannot run on pipelines
Weights should be computed from each fold's own training labels
Manual loops are always faster
Stratified folds are impossible with cross_val_score
questions.explain: Sample weights depend on the class balance of the rows used to fit. Computing them per fold from that fold's training labels keeps each fold's evaluation clean.

questions.q: In the lesson, class_weight="balanced" lowered logistic regression's PR-AUC (0.231 to 0.167). What is the lesson?
options: Class weights never work
PR-AUC is not a valid metric
Logistic regression cannot use weights
Weighting does not automatically improve ranking, so test it rather than assume
questions.explain: Weights mainly shift the decision threshold and can distort the fit. Whether ranking quality improves must be measured.

questions.q: Reviewing 250 alerts caught 44 of 83 frauds. Which statement is right?
options: Precision is 53% and recall is 17.6%
Precision is 17.6% and recall is about 53%
Both precision and recall are 44%
Recall cannot be computed for a review budget
questions.explain: Precision is hits over alerts, 44/250 = 17.6%. Recall is hits over all fraud, 44/83, about 53%.
